title: OBBBA Medicaid Work Requirements + ACA Subsidy Cliff Compound
activeNode: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1 / P.L. 119-21)
catalyst: P.L. 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, mandates 80 hrs/month Medicaid work requirements for the ACA expansion population across 40 states + DC by Jan 1, 2027 (CMS interim final rule, June 1, 2026); several states are implementing earlier on their own timelines. It lands the same year the separate, IRA-era enhanced ACA premium tax credits expired (Dec 31, 2025, unrenewed by Congress) — subsidized marketplace enrollees' average annual premium roughly doubled, from $888 to $1,904. CBO projects ~10M combined coverage losses by 2034. A 25-state-and-DC coalition (Massachusetts leads; CA is a co-plaintiff) is suing CMS (Commonwealth of Massachusetts et al. v. Oz, filed June 29, 2026) over the rule's narrowed 'medically frail' exemption — a federal judge denied the coalition's preliminary injunction on July 29, 2026, so the rule remains in effect while litigation continues. Full state-by-state breakdown and case studies: Special Topics: Access & Cost under OBBBA →
implications: Georgia Pathways to Coverage (GA Dept of Community Health) is the cautionary preview: GAO found $54.2M spent on admin vs. $26.1M on care since 2021, with enrollment still far below the ~246,365-eligible target

Rural hospitals and FQHCs face compounding pressure from coverage loss plus provider-tax/state-directed-payment caps — the $50B Rural Health Transformation Fund is widely expected not to fully offset losses

Medi-Cal plans (San Francisco Health Plan, Partnership HealthPlan of CA) and similar Medicaid MCOs nationally face semi-annual redetermination cycles and rising administrative costs as CA alone estimates up to 3.4M Medi-Cal members at risk

CBO, KFF, and Georgetown University's Center for Children and Families (CCF) become the reference infrastructure most states and hospital associations cite for coverage-loss and state-readiness tracking
State AG litigation (CA-led coalition vs. CMS) creates a live compliance-under-protest dynamic for expansion states — obligations continue during litigation, deferring rather than avoiding exposure
Covered California and other ACA marketplace administrators face enrollment and affordability pressure independent of OBBBA, from the expired enhanced premium tax credits alone

title: IRA Drug Price Negotiation — Cycle 3 Live
catalyst: Cycle 1 prices (10 drugs, 38–79% discounts) took effect Jan 2026. Cycle 3 underway — first-ever Part B drug negotiations and renegotiations; prices effective 2028. CMS-4215-P codification comment period closed Aug 17, 2026.
implications: AbbVie, Merck, Amgen face multi-billion annual Medicare revenue reductions
MA/Part D formulary redesign cascades to PBMs (Capital Rx) and MA plans (SCAN, Oscar, Alignment)
Patient access programs (ConnectiveRx, EVERSANA) restructure as out-of-pocket caps shift manufacturer concession math
Regulatory science firms (Certara) see rising demand as pharma builds evidence for price justification
Companion diagnostics (Guardant) tied to negotiated drugs face formulary and access ripple effects

title: CMS-0057-F Prior Auth APIs — Jan 2027 Deadline
catalyst: Two distinct compliance obligations on different timelines: prior authorization decision timeframes compressed to 72 hours (expedited) and 7 days (standard), effective January 1, 2026; separately, four mandated FHIR APIs (prior auth, provider access, payer-to-payer, patient access) covering MA, Medicaid MCOs, and ACA marketplace plans face a January 1, 2027 buildout deadline.
implications: SCAN, Alignment, Oscar, Partnership HealthPlan, SFHP all face mandated API buildout — IT spend rising
Epic's implementation roadmap becomes a critical dependency for health system compliance
Redox and Smile Digital Health positioned as essential middleware; Notable benefits from PA workflow automation volume
Prior auth denial rates likely to fall as transparency increases — downstream revenue risk for utilization management businesses
CHAI AI governance frameworks become more urgent as payers deploy AI for automated prior auth decisions

title: MA Risk Adjustment Tightening (HCC V28 + RADV)
catalyst: HCC V28 model transition reduces average MA risk scores — compressing plan revenue. RADV extrapolation authority was vacated by the Northern District of Texas (Humana v. Becerra, Sept. 25, 2025) on APA grounds; CMS appealed to the Fifth Circuit (No. 25-11293), with briefing ongoing into 2026 and no ruling yet issued — extrapolation is currently enjoined, not in effect. DOJ scrutiny of retrospective chart chase and upcoding continues separately.
implications: SCAN, Alignment, Oscar face revenue headwinds — per-member-per-month margins under pressure
Coding accuracy programs intensify; risk adjustment vendors (Acumen, RTI) see demand rise
Alignment's owned-provider model provides some insulation; pure plan models (Oscar) more exposed
MA enrollment growth may slow as plans exit unprofitable markets or raise premiums
RTI and CMS contractors evaluating whether V28 achieves intended overbilling correction without overcorrection, while the Fifth Circuit appeal leaves extrapolation authority unresolved

title: TEAM Model — Mandatory Episode Accountability
catalyst: CMS mandatory bundled payment model for 5 surgical episode types (joint replacement, hip femur fracture, spinal fusion, CABG, major bowel procedure) at 721 hospitals across 188 metro areas. No opt-out. Not the first mandatory CMMI model since CJR — ESRD Treatment Choices (2021-2025) was also mandatory. Episodes use a 30-day post-discharge window, shorter than CJR/BPCI Advanced's 90-day window.
implications: AdventHealth and other large health systems in selected markets face direct episode risk
Post-acute referral network optimization becomes a financial imperative — SNF and HH quality differentiation is now contractual
August Health (SNF care management) sees premium on PAC coordination capability
Hinge Health surgical decision support adjacent to TEAM joint replacement episodes
Care navigation for ACO REACH beneficiaries overlapping TEAM episodes creates attribution complexity

title: AI Governance Fragmentation — Federal Floor Contracts as Voluntary Regimes Expand
catalyst: FDA finalized PCCP guidance (Dec 2024) for continuously-learning AI devices; ONC/ASTP proposed HTI-5 (Jan 2026, comment period closed Feb 27, 2026) to remove AI "model card"/transparency requirements added by HTI-1 — a deregulatory reversal, not an expansion, of the federal mandatory leg. CHAI's model-card registry (3,000+ members) partnered with the Joint Commission (Sept 2025) on a certification track for 22,000+ accredited healthcare organizations. The mandatory federal floor is contracting while voluntary (CHAI/TJC) and state-level regimes proliferate without reconciliation.
implications: Health systems (Kaiser, Providence, Cleveland Clinic) face a shifting patchwork rather than a stable set of obligations — ONC's mandatory AI transparency requirement may not survive HTI-5
ModelOp and other CHAI-certified assurance providers compete to operationalize recurring model validation as the de facto trust layer, increasingly by default rather than backstopping a federal floor
Liability for algorithm-driven coverage denials (MA prior-auth) remains unresolved regardless of which regime prevails
State-level AI laws (Utah, Colorado, Texas) add a fourth layer of fragmentation, and become relatively more important if HTI-5 finalizes and narrows the federal mandatory layer
Notable and other AI-enabled clinical automation vendors must track FDA device rules, a possibly-narrowed ONC transparency rule, and CHAI/Joint Commission certification simultaneously
